title: CIA OSI takes UFO research underground, Blue Book as cover

tellings.quote: 1952 the cia's office of scientific intelligence took the real UFO investigations underground they did this while performing a psychological operation the American population in the form of Air Force's Project Blue Book
the long-standing rumors are that this is run by the CIA that in 52 you had public facing UFO UFO research in the form of blue book,
tellings.difference: Framed as long-standing rumor, and credits Battelle and the Atomic Energy Commission.
tellings.link_reason: Both say that in 1952 the CIA ran the real UFO study, with Blue Book as the public-facing front.

as_told.title: CIA running the real UFO study behind Project Blue Book from 1952

tellings.quote: it's now clear in retrospect and I think this is a lot due to Richard Dolan's great research that like you had this cleaving off of the vital study of UFOs the public facing stuff was relegated to project blue book and the air force and then all the private stuff was managed by battel memorial institute

as_told.title: Project Stork and the Battelle split from Blue Book

tellings.quote: With a small staff, the Air Technical Intelligence Center (ATIC) tried to persuade the public that UFOs were not extraordinary.

Although it had monitored UFO reports for at least three years, CIA reacted to the new rash of sightings by forming a special study group within the Office of Scientific Intelligence (OSI) and the Office of Current Intelligence (OCI) to review the situation.
He also urged that CIA conceal its interest from the media and the public, "in view of their probable alarmist tendencies" to accept such interest as confirming the existence of UFOs.
Air Force and CIA officials agreed that outside knowledge of Agency interest in UFOs would make the problem more serious.

plain: In 1952 the CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence, its science analysis branch, took the real UFO investigations underground, while Project Blue Book, the Air Force's public UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, served as a psychological operation on the American people. Michels tells this himself, once calling it a long-standing rumor and once crediting a researcher named Richard Dolan and saying the hidden side was run by the Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research institute, under a project called Stork; if true, the public study was a decoy. A 1997 history published by the CIA and written by the historian Gerald K. Haines says the Office of Scientific Intelligence formed a special study group in 1952, that the agency was urged to "conceal its interest from the media and the public", and that an Air Force intelligence center "tried to persuade the public that UFOs were not extraordinary". It does not say the research went underground or call Blue Book a cover.

discussion.by: CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-90
discussion.text: The teller credits Project Blue Book without naming a record. Gerald Haines's history of the CIA's role in the study of UFOs, published by the CIA in 1997, says OSI formed a study group in 1952 and that the CIA hid its interest in UFOs from the public, and that the Air Force's ATIC "tried to persuade the public that UFOs were not extraordinary"; it does not say the CIA took UFO research underground, and it does not call Blue Book a psychological operation or a cover.
